prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: BACKGROUND-ONLY destination keyframe for a camera approach through the exact supplied STAM lounge. Landscape 16:9.

Use ONLY the supplied original room image as the authoritative reference. Move the VIEWPOINT forward and a little left until a standing visitor is immediately in front of the EXISTING welcome desk's right-hand end, within an arm's reach of its front edge. Maintain approximately the same original viewing direction, with at most a small pan left toward the desk. This is the SAME FIXED ROOM viewed from nearer the desk. No room redesign, no new furniture, no rearrangement, no replacement architecture.

Absolutely NO standing Flight Guide or other foreground character. The existing brunette seated reception employee in the original MUST remain at her original desk position and pose. This is not an empty room and she must not be removed. We will add the standing guide later, after checking the background.

Lock the original room inventory and layout:
1. One curved white/ivory welcome desk on the left, with its original rounded right-hand end and thin warm illuminated lower edge. Same desk length, same end shape, same horizontal shallow top. It is NOT an endless diagonal counter. Camera is now just in front of the existing right end; the near desk front and countertop should fill the lower-left foreground but leave open floor to the right.
2. The ORIGINAL seated brunette reception employee behind its left/central section, now appreciably larger and closer from the approach. Preserve her position relative to the desk, flowers and monitors.
3. Exactly the same TWO compact monitors already on the desk. Preserve their mounting positions, relative separation, orientation, relative heights and workstation arrangement. Both stay on the same original countertop. Show the same visible sides as consistent with a small camera move; do NOT convert them into enormous separated black screens or invent extra stands.
4. The original low white bowl with white orchids at the desk's left stays there. No new desk lamp, glowing cylindrical ornament, extra flowerpot or equipment.
5. The existing silver rounded rectangular glass GATE PORTAL immediately behind the desk's right end remains in precisely that neighboring location. The gate has the SAME curved metal frame, thin warm strips, cyan glass sides and adjoining queue rails. It is larger and closer in this view, just behind the desk toward the image centre. It is NOT moved to the far right, made into a different portal or separated from the desk by a newly invented empty hall.
6. Preserve the tall left window grid, the original outdoor dock and mountains, the central distant double-height glass hall and cyan orbital display, the right-hand information/cinema openings and all main structural arches at their original world positions. Parts may leave the frame naturally through camera movement. Do not move the far hall or add a new building.
7. Existing planting remains at the original positions. No new plants, new queue pattern or additional people.

Physically coherent camera-only movement: foreground desk, nearby receptionist/monitors and nearby portal enlarge and exhibit parallax together; distant hall changes less. Respect occlusion and the original desk-to-gate adjacency. Do not treat the desired close view as a generic newly generated reception room. Do not merely zoom the left corner of the photograph, and do not replace the original scene with a new stylistically similar one.

Keep eye level about 1.65m, a normal 40–45mm lens with straight architectural verticals, same sunlight direction, same photographic materials and warm/cyan accents, natural depth of field with desk workstation and portal legible. This is a clean spatial continuity plate, not a glamour portrait or concept redesign. No interface, hologram UI, labels, captions, arrows, watermark, foreground guide, hands reaching into frame or new objects.
